newsitem.title: USA: GCA May coffee stock data seen mainly neutral.
newsitem.headline: GCA May coffee stock data seen mainly neutral.

text.p: Inventory data released late Monday is likely to have little impact on coffee futures, analysts said, although the slightly smaller-than-expected increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks could provide underlying support in the near-term.
Supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in May by 122,000 60-kg bags, to 1,977,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported after the close on Monday.

Most industry participants had expected aggressive shipments by producers to build U.S. stockpiles by some 150,000-250,000 bags in May, although estimates for an increase ranged broadly from 25,000 to 400,000 bags.

"It is a pretty tepid increase and should strengthen the futures market," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "But I still believe most roasters are covered and I would not look for much of an impact."
The port of New Orleans posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. New Orleans stocks rose by 101,000 bags to 853,000 bags, the GCA said.
Inventories increased by 32,000 bags, to 289,000 bags in New York. Warehouse stocks in Miami also increased in May, rising 23,000 bags to 142,000 bags.
In Laredo, Texas, however, inventories decreased by 30,000 bags, to 248,000 bags, while Houston stockpiles were down 29,000 bags in May, to 92,000 bags.

But while the modest increase in monthly consumer coffee stocks could be viewed as constructive, some traders said the latest production estimate from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) may offset any bullish sentiment.

"Stocks were at the lower end of expectations, but I do not think the market is going to respond to the GCA report," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "Their number was overshadowed by the USDA report that said there will be more coffee coming out next season."

After Friday's close, the USDA forecast world coffee production in 1997/98 to come in at 103.7 million bags, compared with 100.7 million bags the previous season. USDA estimated the 1997/98 Brazil crop would come in at 28 million bags, versus 27.5 million bags in 1996/97.
Traders are now monitoring CSCE certified stocks ahead of the spot July contract's first notice day on June 20.
The most significant thing now is the delivery of July and the certifieds," said one trader. "With the July-September spread coming in so much, it may not attract a lot of coffee to the exchange."

The CSCE reported after Monday's close that stocks certified for delivery against the exchange rose by 3,520 bags as of June 13, to 48,050 bags -- or the equivalent of about 171 lots. Meanwhile, July open interest stood at 4,926 lots as of Friday.
